summary: Hideki Yukawa (1907–1981) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and Osaka University (~1934–1938), later holding posts at Osaka, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Columbia universities.

Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Women's University.

Hidenori Sakuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later teaching at International Buddhist University, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho and Waseda universities. He served as a professor at Waseda University (1968–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University, among other leadership roles.
Hideo Murai works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a professor at Otani University and a committee member of the Otani Academic Society.

Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He held positions at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies and Taisho University during the 1990s.
Hidetaka Fukazawa (born 1956) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1975–1980) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1997.
Hidetaka Nakatani is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under supervisor Gadjin M. Nagao.
Hideto Ono (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University in 1991.
Hidetomo Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Taisho University, where he has held roles as a researcher, lecturer, and chief research fellow between 1998 and 2017.
Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). He held academic posts at Tohoku University, Osaka University, Tokyo Institute of Technology, and the University of Tokyo.

Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1973–1982) and later served there as assistant professor (1991) and professor of Indian Philosophy (~1996–2019).
Hideyuki Matsumori works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University, where he was attested as an assistant professor in 2015.
Hildegard Diemberger (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology. She completed supervised research under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner.

Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) specializes in Indology and archaeology. She studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she was an associate professor (~1980–2012), later chairing the National Monuments Authority (2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810) and held a post at the University of Breslau from circa 1813 to 1861.

Hiram W. Woodward is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and Yale. He taught at Silpakorn, Michigan, and Vermont, and served as curator of Asian Art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at DAV College, Lahore, Oriental College, and Panjab University. He held positions with the Archaeological Survey of India and served as Baroda State's Director of Archaeology (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and held a research post at Taisho University.

Hirofumi Isoda (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1961–1966), where he later taught, and is an honorary professor at Shimane University.
